overall.summary: Every stored number reproduces and the structure is sound, but the record's overall reading that o on d1 is the model's strongest single penalty (and that column d matters 'especially' at d1) is contradicted by the model: d1 is the weakest of the four lower centre-column squares, and in legal positions swapping colours between d1 and d3 moves the score 4.3 log-odds in favour of d3. Two leaf hypotheses misdescribe where their squares are.

findings.statement: x pieces in column d, especially on the bottom centre square d1 and on d2 and d3, raise the predicted chance ... o pieces there lower it, with o on d1 the strongest single penalty
findings.check: colour flip of each occupied square over the training rows (x minus o, whole-model log-odds), and legal swaps of colours between d1 and another occupied square
findings.evidence: whole-model flip: d3 +7.54 (n 7713), c3 +4.75, d2 +4.25, e3 +3.91, d4 +3.25, d1 only +1.94 (n 30872), the smallest of d1-d4. Legal swap over the 4457 rows with d1 and d3 of opposite colours: (o on d1, x on d3) scores 4.83 vs 0.52 for (x on d1, o on d3), +4.31 log-odds in favour of d3; over 9260 rows with d1/d2 opposite, x on d2 beats x on d1 by 1.50. So o on d3 (and d2) is a larger penalty than o on d1; d1 is not 'especially' important in the whole model. The large d1 effect of part A (+3.28) is partly cancelled by low_board_mixed (-1.69), upper_rows_mixed (-0.82) and second_row_centre (-0.48).

findings.statement: the model tracks who controls the centre column d, with a strong reward for x and a strong penalty for o on the bottom centre square d1
findings.check: column-control subgroups for every column; colour flips and legal swaps (as V6)
findings.evidence: centre-column part holds (column d spread 98% / 67% / 27%, the widest of the seven columns; outcome rates 98% / 68% / 28%). The d1 emphasis is overstated: d1's whole-model effect (+1.94 log-odds) is smaller than d2 (+4.25), d3 (+7.54), d4 (+3.25), c3, e3 and the edge squares a1 (-3.17), g1 (-3.05). Evidence numbers (2710/98%, 29186/67%/68%, 2708/27%/28%, row 15070 swap 12% -> 76%, five ablation AUCs, affine 0.855) all reproduce.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --hold row:15070 --set c_d1=1 --set c_a1=-1
uv run python -m explaneat verify linearise <T>

findings.statement: rewards x pieces in the centre of the bottom row over pieces near the left edge (d1 vs b1)
findings.check: colour flip per bottom-row square for this part
findings.evidence: numbers reproduce (3.58/2.31, 1.88/3.31, row 15069 1.09 -> 2.91, 67% -> 98%, AUC 0.853; output weights all positive; row 1 = 70% of input variance). But the part's bottom-row profile is c1 +1.17, d1 +1.66 against a1 -0.85, b1 -1.05, e1 -2.06, f1 -1.49, g1 -0.51: x just right of centre (e1, f1) is penalised more than x near the left edge, and its largest common-square effects are g3 (-2.44) and e1 (-2.06). 'Over pieces near the left edge' describes only part of the contrast; it is c1/d1 against the rest of the bottom row, the right side most.

bottom_row_centre_A.why: Penalising o on the bottom centre square d1 is a centre-control reading, and d1 is the part's largest effect among commonly occupied squares (+3.28 log-odds, x minus o), with 75% of its input variance from the bottom row.

bottom_row_centre_B.why: It rewards x on c1/d1, but it penalises x just right of centre (e1, f1) more than near the left edge, and its largest common effects (g3, e1) are not in the stated d1-versus-b1 reading.

low_board_mixed.why: x on d2 is its strongest effect, but it also rewards o on c1 and x off d1, corrections with no game reading, as the hypothesis itself says.

second_row_centre.why: A 'x stacked on the left-centre squares' reading holds (b3, c3, c2, d3, b4, a4), but the stated location ('just above the bottom row', columns b to d) is wrong for b3/d3 and omits its largest square c3.

upper_rows_mixed.why: x on d3 is confirmed as a centre-column reward, but the equally large b3 penalty is a correction with no game meaning, as the hypothesis itself says.
